- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent periods; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust downward by 1–4% if recent sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is stable or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (e.g., alternating 0.67/0.33), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
